'''Giovanna Morigi''' (born 1969) is a physicist whose research involves theoretical [[quantum mechanics]], including [[quantum optics]], [[Wigner crystal]]s, [[laser cooling]], and [[ultracold atom]]s.{{r|cr}} Beyond fundamental physics, she has also published research on size control in biological [[tissue growth]].{{r|size}} Born in Italy and educated in [[Austria]], she works in Germany as a professor of theoretical physics at [[Saarland University]].

==Education and career==
Morigi was born in 1969 in [[Ravenna]],{{r|gnd}} and was a student at the Liceo Scientifico "A. Oriani" in [[Ravenna]].{{r|cr}} After earning a [[laurea]] at the [[University of Pisa]] in 1995, and spending a year as a researcher at the [[Clarendon Laboratory]] of the [[University of Oxford]],{{r|orcid}} she completed a PhD in 1999 at the [[University of Innsbruck]].{{r|inspire}}

She became a postdoctoral researcher at the [[Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics]] from 2001 to 2002, continuing there as a research associate while taking a position as assistant professor at the [[University of Ulm]] from 2002 to 2004. She was a [[Ramón y Cajal (scholarship)|Ramón y Cajal Fellow]] at the [[Autonomous University of Barcelona]] from 2004 to 2009, when she took her present position as a [[full professor]] at Saarland University.{{r|orcid}}

==Recognition==
Morigi was named as a 2022 [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] (APS), after a nomination from the APS Division of Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics, "for the invention of novel techniques for cooling trapped ions, atoms, and [[Molecule|molecules]], and for pioneering theoretical work on the structural phase transitions in low-dimensional trapped-ion crystals".{{r|cr|faps}}
